title: automation: a `map` or `subflow` node drops its child run's refusal, so a refused write deep in a flow reaches the caller as the raw node chain
body:
domain:ui#4 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbDAucNyQ4UtzCJKyh

carries item 2 of #27487 (the server half: the refusal must cross `map` / `subflow`); #27487 keeps item 1 (the console action door reads the refusal the server sends).

Filing gate: ① product defect, user-visible, split from #27487 by the `domain:ui` seat that dispatched it (the card thread measured both halves before its first edit).

## Business reason

Who: any console user who runs a flow-backed action (or a record-triggered / API-triggered flow) whose refused write sits inside a `map` item or a `subflow`. What happens today: the refusal is correct, but the caller gets the whole engine chain as the message, e.g. the showcase "Recalculate Estimate" as a `member`: `Node 'recalc_each' failed: map 'recalc_each': item 0 (subflow 'showcase_recalc_task_estimate') failed: Node 'write_estimate' failed: update_record(showcase_task) failed: You do not have permission to perform this action. …`. Without the fix the console can never show the plain refusal for these flows, whatever the ui does: there is no structured refusal in the answer to read.

## Where (measured on `origin/main` `4a00b2b7`)

- `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/map-node.ts` ~L219–222: `if (!child.success) return { success: false, error: \`map '…': item N (subflow '…') failed: ${child.error}\` … }` — the child run's `innerRefusal` / `userMessage` are not carried onto the returned failure.
- `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/subflow-node.ts` ~L169–172: the same for `subflow`.
- `packages/services/service-automation/src/inner-refusal.ts` (header of `CARRIED_REFUSAL`, ~L120–124) records the current behaviour: "A container that re-words a child failure into a NEW returned failure of its own (`try_catch` with no catch region, `subflow`) builds a new error, and the brand does not cross it; the run's result then carries no member". That is the gap: the one-level case already carries `innerRefusal` / `userMessage` on the 400 `FLOW_FAILED` (`endpoint-executor.ts` ~L590), the nested case does not.

## Acceptance

- A refused write inside a `map` item or a `subflow` reaches the run's result (and the 400 `FLOW_FAILED` envelope) with the child's `innerRefusal` / `userMessage`, exactly as the one-level case does; the `error` text may stay as it is.
- Pinned by an engine test per container (`map`, `subflow`, map → subflow nested) asserting the carried members.
- No new refusal vocabulary: the existing carriage (`attachCarriedRefusal`) only crosses the two containers.

## Reader who acts

The lane triage assigns (the fix lands in `packages/services/service-automation`). The `domain:ui` half (#27487 item 1) lands first with a pin on the envelope shape this card will produce.

## reach

Public door: the console record header ⋯ action "Recalculate Estimate" on `examples/app-showcase` as a `member` (repro on #27487), and `POST /api/v1/apps/showcase/recalc` (declared `type: 'flow'` endpoint) answering 400 `FLOW_FAILED` with no `innerRefusal`.

## Dedupe

Search API is unavailable from this session; read instead: the 500 most recently created issues (open and closed) by title, grep `subflow|map node|map '|inner.?refusal|carriedRefusal|refusal.*(flow|node)` → 2 hits: #27487 (the parent, ui half) and #27381 (refusal wording a package cannot reach: state_machine holes, joined validation messages, screen-flow successMessage — a different gap). No duplicate.
